_meta.title: <ORG> fleet registry
_doc: TEMPLATE. Rename to REGISTRY.json and replace the placeholders. This file is the source of truth for
WHO runs (agents[]), WHEN (registration.cron, in schedule_tz), UNDER WHICH NAME they log
(history_identity + history_aliases), and WHO MAY WRITE WHAT (state_files). scripts/state_io.py
enforces state_files; scripts/fleet_watch.py reads the schedules; scripts/registry_stubs.py renders
the scheduler stubs from it. Edit this file, never the stubs.
A 'beat' is one routine prompt registered several times on different schedules, each with its own
id, history_identity and (optionally) a `beat` value the routine branches on. Beats share an owner
through agent_aliases, so any beat may write the routine's files; they do NOT share a run counter.
agents[].history_aliases = spelling variants of THAT agent's own identity (used by the run counter
and the liveness check). agent_aliases (top level) = the routine's alias GROUP across beats (used by
ownership and the inbox). Keep the two distinct: merging them lets one beat's run mask another's silence.
_meta.schedule_tz: <IANA timezone, e.g. Europe/London - every cron below is local to this>

registration.schedule_human: daily 07:15, after the overnight agents and before the briefing

state/history.jsonl.note: one line per run via log_run(); decisions required

state/_writes.jsonl.note: audit sidecar written by the helper; never by hand

state/escalations.json.note: everyone else: raise_escalation() -> bus -> folded by the owner

state/validate_baseline.json.note: written by validate_state.py during the guard run

state/decisions/.note: session captures; agents only touch frontmatter via mark_decision_delivered()

state/legacy_counters.json.note: example of a retired file nobody may write
